item.title: [7] Moir\'e metals and continuum models beyond a single valley
item.description:
Last authors: Andrew Klekovkin-Hardy, Valentin Cr\'epel

Authors: Matthew Albert, Andrew Klekovkin-Hardy, Valentin Cr\'epel

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Continuum model for moiré NbSe2 relevant to CDW and superconducting instabilities.

Tags: #theory #NbSe2 #moire

Abstract: We derive continuum models of moir\'e materials valid over the full monolayer Brillouin zone, as required for metals whose large Fermi surfaces are not confined to a single valley. To this end, we introduce an environment-resolved two-center approximation, in which each hopping amplitude depends not only on the distance between the orbitals it connects but also on its position within the moir\'e cell. Taking the local environment to be set by the disregistry of the two layers alone, these moir\'e couplings and their full set of harmonics can be learnt from commensurate bilayers at uniform stackings, without fitting. The method shows excellent agreement with ab initio band structures on moir\'e cells containing a few hundred atoms. Applied to twisted NbSe$_2$, it yields a continuum model in which moir\'e effects concentrate at the van Hove singularities, a single-particle starting point for studying moir\'e-tuned superconducting, charge-density-wave instabilities and their competition.

item.title: [10] Anisotropic spin splitting in -MnTe epilayers on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates
item.description:
Last authors: Tomasz Wojtowicz, Valentine V. Volobuev

Authors: Zofia Kopacz-Maj, Ali Akbar, Aleksandr Kazakov, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: ARPES study of altermagnetic spin splitting in MnTe; direct match for user specialty.

Tags: #method #material #topic

Abstract: $\alpha$-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial $\alpha$-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the $\Gamma$-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along $\Gamma$-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for $\alpha$-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.

item.title: [7] Quantum Monte-Carlo study of spin-valley ferromagnetism in rhombohedral graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Tobias M. R. Wolf, Chunli Huang

Authors: Michael Demos, Dongqi Li, Mainak Das, Tobias M. R. Wolf, Chunli Huang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of magnetic order in graphene, related to STM and Pomeranchuk effect experiments.

Tags: #theory #graphene #ferromagnetism

Abstract: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at $T_c \approx 0.7$ K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.

item.title: [9] Intertwined ferromagnetic and altermagnetic orders in Cr-doped MnTe
item.description:
Last authors: Juan Carlos Idrobo, Jiun-Haw Chu

Authors: Jonathan M. DeStefano, Yaofeng Xie, Guodong Ren, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of altermagnetism and ferromagnetism in doped MnTe, a key material of interest.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #material #altermagnetism #ferromagnetism

Abstract: Ferromagnetism and altermagnetism both break time-reversal symmetry, yet their distinct transformation properties under crystalline symmetries forbid direct bilinear coupling between their order parameters. Whether these two magnetic orders can remain thermodynamically distinct while strongly influencing one another remains an open question. Here we demonstrate the homogeneous coexistence of ferromagnetism and altermagnetism in Cr-doped MnTe. By tuning the ferromagnetic ordering temperature across the nearly unchanged N\'eel temperature with Cr doping, we uncover a striking interplay between the two orders: the ferromagnetic transition becomes a crossover when altermagnetism develops first, whereas the onset of altermagnetism strongly suppresses the out-of-plane ferromagnetic remanence when ferromagnetism develops first. Moreover, spin-orbit coupling enables symmetry-selective interactions through which the ferromagnetic moment controls the altermagnetic domain manifold, with its out-of-plane and in-plane components biasing the time-reversal ($Z_2$) and orientational ($Z_3$) sectors, respectively. Our results reveal how two symmetry-distinct magnetic orders can retain separate ordering tendencies while remaining strongly coupled, providing a route towards internal control of altermagnetic domain states.

item.title: [7] Temperature Evolution of Magnon-Polarons in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet FePS3
item.description:
Last authors: E. Karpierz-Marczewska, M. Potemski

Authors: A. Krajewska, J. Kierdaszuk, M. Dub, E. Karpierz-Marczewska, M. Potemski

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Raman study of magnon-phonon coupling in a vdW antiferromagnet.

Tags: #material #van-der-waals #antiferromagnetism

Abstract: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the N\'eel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. The corresponding magnetic field decreases from approximately 13 T at 4 K to 5.6 T at 85 K, bringing the effect within reach of a standard laboratory magnet. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.

item.title: [7] Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
item.description:
Last authors: Massimiliano Stengel, Samuel Ponc\'e

Authors: Jae-Mo Lihm, Malte R\"osner, Cyrus E. Dreyer, Massimiliano Stengel, Samuel Ponc\'e

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Advanced DFT methodology for dynamical screening in TaS2, relevant for CDW and electronic structure spectroscopy.

Tags: #theory #TaS2 #electronic-structure

Abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. We use it to compute the total dynamical electron-electron interaction, including direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions with dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon couplings, all on equal footing. In hole-doped monolayer hBN, the hybridization of the carrier plasmon with the longitudinal optical phonon makes the low-energy retarded interaction nonmonotonic in the carrier density, an effect missed by the adiabatic approximation. In metallic monolayer TaS2, nonadiabatic effects are weak and occur only due to the intraband electron-hole continuum and the nesting of nearly parallel Fermi velocities. We also validate the widely used screened-screened approximation for the phonon spectral function. This work opens the way to first-principles studies of spectral functions, transport, and superconductivity with dynamically screened interactions.

item.title: [7] Frustration-Induced 1/6-Vortex-Paired Phase in a Kagome XY Model
item.description:
Last authors: Tong-Yu Lin, Guang-Ming Zhang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of fractional vortices in kagome systems, matching user focus on frustrated lattices.

Tags: #theory #kagome #magnetism

Abstract: Geometric frustration can fractionalize vortices in two-dimensional XY systems, but a given frustrated model usually hosts only a single type of fractional vortex. Here we study a kagome XY model in which an antiferromagnetic coupling $J_1$ and a second-harmonic coupling $K$ favor two competing frustrated ground-state manifolds. For $K/J_1<1/9$, the ground states map onto those of the kagome three-state Potts antiferromagnet and support $1/3$ vortices; for $K/J_1>1/9$, they map onto those of the kagome Ising antiferromagnet and support $1/2$ vortices. At $K/J_1=1/9$, the two manifolds become degenerate, and bends in the domain walls between them carry $1/6$-vortex excitations. Tensor-network calculations show that a finite-temperature phase with quasi-long-range order only in $e^{6i\theta}$ emerges from this degenerate point, separating the $1/3$- and $1/2$-vortex-paired phases. This $1/6$-vortex-paired phase has no counterpart in either parent manifold, showing that competing frustrated manifolds provide a route to new fractional-vortex-paired phases.

item.title: [8] Quantum-Geometric Subgap Second-Harmonic Generation in PT-Symmetric Antiferromagnetic Insulators
item.description:
Last authors: Shakeel Ahmad, Fei Xue

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates quantum geometry and topological phases in MnBi2Te4 bilayers, a material of direct interest.

Tags: #theory #MnBi2Te4 #topological

Abstract: Although quantum geometry plays an established role in electronic transport and optical responses, the contribution of the time-reversal-odd Riemannian connection to fully subgap responses remains less explored. Here we identify intrinsic second-harmonic generation in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets, predominantly governed by the real sector of the interband Hermitian connection and arising entirely from virtual interband transitions. In bilayer MnBi$_2$Te$_4$, the response persists in trivial phases but is enhanced in the layer-Chern phase and reverses sign with N\'eel order, offering a probe of quantum geometry and phase-sensitive readout of antiferromagnetic order without mobile carriers or real excitations.

item.title: [9] Berry curvature quadrupole induced third-order anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic KV2Se2O
item.description:
Last authors: Zhichao Guo, Hua Wang

Authors: Jiacheng Yao, Zhuocheng Lu, Zhichao Guo, Hua Wang

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit on altermagnetism, Berry curvature, and anomalous Hall effect in a specific compound.

Tags: #theory #KV2Se2O #altermagnetism

Abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, providing a symmetry-rich platform for exploring nonlinear quantum-geometric transport. In the d-wave altermagnet considered here, the antiunitary symmetry operation $TC_{4z}$ enforces a vanishing momentum-integrated Berry curvature, while inversion symmetry forbids a finite Berry-curvature dipole. Consequently, the Berry curvature quadrupole (BCQ) can provide a contribution to the nonlinear Hall response, scaling as $\tau^2$, where $\tau$ denotes the relaxation time. We derive a gauge-covariant Wannier interpolation formula that enables efficient evaluation of the BCQ directly from first-principles Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians. Applying this framework to $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$, we calculate the momentum-space distribution of the BCQ and the associated chemical potential dependent nonlinear conductivity. The momentum-resolved analysis reveals that the dominant contribution originates from spin-orbit coupling induced avoided arossings, directly linking the gap structure to the sign-changing nonlinear response. Our work establishes a general first-principles route to higher-order quantum-geometric responses in altermagnets, opening avenues for exploring nonlinear Hall effects in next-generation spintronic and magnetoelectronic devices.

item.title: [9] Multiband-Induced Complex Magnetotransport in the Kagome Metal LuNb6Sn6
item.description:
Last authors: Quansheng Wu, Mingquan He

Authors: Hongye Zhang, Xingyu Ma, Ying Zhu, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: kagome metal

Tags: #kagome #chargedensitywave #CDW #anomalousHall #transport

Abstract: We report the electrical transport properties of the kagome metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$, which undergoes a charge density wave (CDW) transition at $T_\mathrm{CDW}\approx80$ K. Similar to the kagome metals $A$V$_3$Sb$_5$ ($A$ = K, Rb, Cs), LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$ develops complex magnetotransport behavior near and below the CDW transition. In particular, the longitudinal magnetoconductivity exhibits an approximately linear field dependence below about 1 T, whereas the field dependence of Hall conductivity displays pronounced nonlinearity and a field-induced sign reversal. Although an anomalous Hall-like contribution can be extracted by subtracting a local background from the Hall conductivity, mobility-spectrum analysis shows that the overall magnetotransport can be largely accounted for by multiband conduction involving high-mobility electronlike and holelike carriers. Nevertheless, sizable deviations from the multiband model emerge near $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, pointing to additional CDW-related scattering processes. These results demonstrate that high-mobility multiband transport, together with CDW-induced modifications of carrier scattering, play important roles in the complex magnetotransport of LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$.

item.title: [7] Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction (Carbon)
item.description:
Last authors: Sarah J. Haigh, Kostya S. Novoselov

Authors: Tatiana Latychevskaia, Colin Robert Woods, Yi Bo Wang, et al.

Published as: Carbon DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental CBED study on graphene and hBN, relevant to user interest in 2D heterostructures.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #microscopy

Abstract: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. The scattering parameters recovered from the experimental CBED patterns of graphene and twisted graphene-hBN structure show good agreement with the theoretically obtained values.

item.title: [8] Mirror-symmetry engineering of altermagnetism based on monolayer hexagonal lattices
item.description:
Last authors: Han-Bing Li, Zhi-Gang Shao

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Proposes a design principle for altermagnetism in 2D hexagonal lattices, directly relevant to user interests.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #monolayer

Abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. Abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. item.title: [7] Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
item.description:
Last authors: Long Zhang, Zhanghai Chen

Authors: Yuxin Duan, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental work on van der Waals heterostructures and many-body interactions.

Tags: #experiment #vanderWaals #many-body

Abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

item.description:
Last authors: Matthew Brahlek, Liang Wu

Authors: Benjamin F. Mead, Isaiah Gray, Seng Huat Lee, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly explores circular dichroism and anomalous Hall in a high-interest altermagnet material MnTe.

Tags: #experiment #MnTe #altermagnetism

Abstract: Altermagnetism has emerged as a new class of magnetism with vanishing magnetization and macroscopic time reversal symmetry breaking. Hexagonal MnTe is a g-wave altermagnet with a 307 K N\'eel temperature, large spin splitting, and an anomalous Hall effect. However, the relationship between altermagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect in MnTe remains debated. Here, using optical magnetic circular dichroism, we observe hysteresis and a memory effect in a MnTe bulk crystal below 250 K. No hysteresis is seen after polishing the bulk crystal and in thin films. We conclude that the hysteresis in magnetic circular dichroism in the bulk crystal is from surface defects. item.description:
Last authors: Dieter Koelle, Wolfgang Lang

Authors: Bernd Aichner, Christoph Schmid, Sandra Keppert, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental vortex dynamics study in a classic high-Tc cuprate relevant to unconventional SC interests.

Tags: #experiment #Bi2212 #superconductivity

Abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. item.description:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Luca Banszerus

Authors: Emma Horgan, Bernd Aichner, Nadine Omar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Luca Banszerus

Abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $\mu$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

Last authors: Myoung-Woo Yoo, Axel Hoffmann

Abstract: Current-driven magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for fast spintronic devices, yet their transient dynamics are not yet fully understood. item.title: [10] Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Zhiyuan Sun, Shuyun Zhou

Authors: Fei Wang, Xuanxi Cai, Wanying Chen, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Shuyun Zhou

Tags: #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #Dirac #Berrycurvature #Chern #graphene #monolayer #topological

Abstract: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap-the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase-has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.

Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, hosting topological order and fractionalized anyonic excitations. item.title: [7] Chiral Majorana hinge modes on a curved surface with magnetic impurities
item.description:
Last authors: Sin\'ead M. Griffin, Luca Chirolli

Authors: Ilyoun Na, James G. McHugh, Sin\'ead M. Griffin, Luca Chirolli

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant theoretical study of Majorana modes in topological superconductors with magnetic interaction.

Tags: #topology #Majorana #superconduct

Abstract: Chiral Majorana modes, a key ingredient for topological quantum computation, arise on the surface of a three-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological superconductor when a magnetic field induces a sign-changing surface mass. In practice, the orbital response of the superconductor tilts the surface spectrum and overwhelms the Zeeman term as the field grows. Here we show that magnetic impurities on a spherical surface can instead generate this mass term through their exchange coupling, so that only a weak field is required. The Ising surface Majorana modes mediate a ferromagnetic Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, derived here on the curved surface, that orders the radial impurity moments into an inversion-breaking hedgehog at zero field. An axial field instead stabilizes a domain wall across which the radial magnetization reverses sign, leaving a single chiral Majorana mode along the equator and realizing an inversion-protected second-order topological superconductor.

item.title: [8] Topological spin textures in an antiferromagnetic monolayer
item.description:
Last authors: Stefan Heinze, Kirsten von Bergmann

Authors: Felix Zahner, Tim Drevelow, Roberto Lo Conte, Roland Wiesendanger, Stefan Heinze, Kirsten von Bergmann

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STM observation of topological spin textures in magnetic monolayers; high experimental relevance.

Tags: #STM #monolayer #topology #antiferromagnet

Abstract: Topological spin structures such as magnetic skyrmions are of fundamental interest and promising for various types of applications in spintronics. Skyrmions have been predicted to emerge also in antiferromagnetic materials where they exhibit superior transport properties. They were experimentally revealed in synthetic antiferromagnets, however, still remain elusive in intrinsic atomic antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate how topological spin structures can be stabilized in an antiferromagnetic monolayer. Using spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe an antiferromagnetic spin spiral in the Mn monolayer and a collinear antiferromagnetic state in the Mn double-layer on Ta(110). Near the boundary to the double-layer spin structures equivalent to half of an antiferromagnetic skyrmion form in the monolayer as revealed in combination with first-principles calculations and micromagnetic simulations. Our simulations show how the topological state in antiferromagnetic material systems can be controlled by the configuration within a lateral heterostructure, resulting in trivial non-coplanar states or antiferromagnetic skyrmions.

item.title: [7] Stacking-Directed Polarization and Excitonic Engineering in MoS2/MoSe2 van der Waals Heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Mohammed El Amine Miloudi, Oliver K\"uhn

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Detailed study of 2D van der Waals heterostructures; directly relevant to electronic structure/spectroscopy.

Tags: #vanderWaals #heterostructure #electronic-structure

Abstract: The stacking-dependent polarization and excitonic response of MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterostructures were investigated using GW+BSE many-body perturbation theory. While homobilayer MoS$_2$ exhibited a switchable interlayer dipole driven by registry-induced symmetry breaking, the MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ hetero-interface remained pinned by the intrinsic chemical potential mismatch between sulfur and selenium. In 2L-MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ trilayers, the stacking sequence enabled a deterministic control of photogenerated electrons between the central and bottom MoS$_2$ layers, governed by internal electric fields and quasiparticle band-edge shifts of 60--70~meV. Our calculations predicted a 36~meV interlayer excitonic shift, in remarkable agreement with recent experiments. These results elucidate the microscopic link between atomic registry and many-body interactions, establishing transition metal dichalcogenide trilayers as a potential platform for sliding ferroelectricity and programmable optoelectronic functionalities.

item.title: [8] Emergent Skyrmion Hall Effect in d-wave Altermagnets at Finite Temperature
item.description:
Last authors: Yang Liu, Minghui Qin

Authors: Tingting Liu, Bingyu Sun, Fengyue Zhu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to altermagnetism and transport phenomena in magnetic materials.

Tags: #altermagnet #transport #magnetic

Abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with unconventional symmetry-dependent responses, offering a promising platform for spintronic applications. Here, we show that a voltage-controlled magnetic-anisotropy gradient drives altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions in a nearly rectilinear, Hall-free manner in the absence of thermal fluctuations, owing to their strongly compensated gyrotropic response. Thermal magnons qualitatively modify this behavior by increasing the longitudinal drag through magnon--skyrmion scattering and generating a transverse reaction force through handedness-dependent skew scattering. Owing to the anisotropic altermagnetic magnon band structure, the relative transport weights of the two magnon handednesses are interchanged between propagation along the $x$ and $y$ directions, resulting in transverse skyrmion drifts of opposite sign. By contrast, along the high-symmetry direction, the two magnon handednesses remain degenerate and their transverse contributions cancel, preserving Hall-free motion even at finite temperature. We thus uncover a thermally emergent anisotropic skyrmion Hall effect whose direction-dependent magnitude and sign originate from the intrinsic symmetry-dependent magnon spectrum, making it a generic finite-temperature dynamical feature of ATM skyrmions. Our results establish a low-power route toward electrically controlled and thermally tunable ATM skyrmion transport.

item.title: [7] Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
item.description:
Last authors: Seth Ariel Tongay, Itai Epstein

Authors: Saroj Poudyal, Anabel Atash Kahlon, Michael Klein, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Optical enhancement of excitonic response in vdW heterostructures.

Tags: #vdW #excitons #photonics

Abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.

item.title: [7] Resonant suppression of the -type Josephson component in a Kitaev-ladder junction
item.description:
Last authors: Hiroki Tsuchiura, Yukio Tanaka

Authors: Cheng-Rong Xie, Hiroki Tsuchiura, Yukio Tanaka

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Topological superconductivity and Josephson transport relevant to Majorana physics.

Tags: #superconduct #topological #transport

Abstract: We study how discrete normal-segment levels control equilibrium Josephson transport between two Kitaev-ladder superconductors. Away from resonance, detuning opens a selective-clamping window: inter-leg hybridization removes the phase dependence of a $0$-favoring low-energy ground-state contribution while retaining a competing $\pi$-favoring contribution, allowing a smooth negative first harmonic even for bulk-topologically trivial leads. At resonance and $\phi=\pi$, an exact collective-clamping identity makes both low-energy ground-state contributions phase independent above a threshold, although individual quasiparticle levels can remain dispersive. Finite-energy quasiparticles then produce a positive residual first harmonic in a controlled sweet-point regime. For fixed $0<\phi<\pi$, helicity mixing instead yields a positive resonant low-energy harmonic in the weak-coupling limit. Exact identities, fourth-order sign rules, and recursive Green-function calculations establish how resonant alignment changes the spectral contributions governing Josephson phase selection.

item.title: [9] Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid
item.description:
Last authors: Allan MacDonald, Ali Yazdani

Authors: Ryan L. Lee, Jungwoo Lee, Viliam Va\v{n}o, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Ali Yazdani

Tags: #graphene #superconduct #Landaulevel

Abstract: Lattices of quantized vortices are a defining property of rotating superfluids and of type-II superconductors in magnetic fields. Realizing an analogous vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid-formed from bound electron-hole pairs-has remained challenging because excitons are electrically neutral. Building on previous theoretical studies of the low-energy excitations in an exciton superfluid, recent theory has predicted that in a strong magnetic field, a weakly charged exciton superfluid can stabilize a vortex-antivortex lattice arising from the mutual repulsion of fractionally charged vortex cores. Here we report evidence for this predicted vortex lattice in a bilayer exciton condensate by imaging its charged vortices with the scanning tunnelling microscope. The condensate forms between Landau levels of two graphene layers separated by a thin hexagonal boron nitride barrier in a perpendicular magnetic field. We find that the vortex lattice periodicity scales with the total excess charge and is insensitive to its distribution between the two layers, in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Our observations provide evidence for phase coherence in an exciton superfluid system.

item.title: [7] Quantum Noise Spectroscopy of Nanoscale Charge Defects in Silicon Carbide at Room Temperature (Sci. Adv.)
item.description:
Last authors: Qi Zhang, Fazhan Shi

Authors: Jinpeng Liu, Yuanhong Teng, Yu Chen, et al.

Published as: Sci. Adv. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study using quantum sensing to probe charge dynamics in semiconductors.

Tags: #experiment #charge-dynamics

Abstract: The nanoscale charge environment critically influences the performance of semiconductor devices, yet traditional characterization techniques usually lack the spatial resolution to resolve nanoscale charge heterogeneity and identify microscopic noise sources. Here, we address this critical gap by utilizing individual PL5 color centers in commercial silicon carbide as room-temperature, broadband (near-DC to GHz) quantum spectrometers. We report the first real-time, nanoscale observation of single-charge tunneling dynamics at room temperature in 4H-SiC by monitoring the random telegraph noise using optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR). This capability enables an electrical noise imaging technique that shows distinct noise variations on different wafers. Employing dynamical decoupling and $T_1$ relaxation spectroscopy, we observe correlations of noise spectral density across frequency bands and obtain the nanoscale electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) fingerprint of spin defects in SiC. Ultimately, through surface chemical engineering, we identify the native oxide layer as the main source of resolved electromagnetic fluctuations. This work establishes a versatile atomic-scale metrology platform bridging quantum sensing and semiconductor engineering, offering critical insights for optimizing third-generation semiconductor interfaces and advancing solid-state quantum technologies.
